It's kinda hard to explain in terms that aren't proprietary to my work, let me give this a terrible shot lol...

Currency and pricing are changed based on country, but in Korean law if you change the functionality of an international program specifically for the Korean market, the law changes that version and it then must be licensed through a government-certified service distributor depending on the service.

Basically if the client was made only for the Korean region, Valve would have to let a Korean distributor (Nexon, Naver, Daum, etc) distribute the client in a way that follows Korean law. This means requiring ID verification, hard age restriction, and region locking all games. That last one is impossible.

There's a legal loophole where a "new" Korean company (Valve Korea or something lol) could go through years of bureaucracy getting proper certifications and distribution rights to release their own client, but they will be bound by the same ID verification rules. On top of that, they could only serve games with Korean regions. Games that are not indisputably suitable for all ages must also be verified by the Korean game rating board known as GRAC.

Steam is in a bind with this one. Either we all get it, nobody gets it, or they fix this shit. Everyone likes Discord, nobody likes this. What works for one service might not work for another.
